name: ASXL transcriptional regulator 1

function.text: ASXL1 encodes a chromatin-regulatory protein involved in controlling histone modifications and transcriptional programs, including those governing hematopoietic differentiation.

germline.text: Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to Bohring-Opitz syndrome (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Reported somatic alteration contexts include MDS/MPN, NOS; Primary myelofibrosis; Systemic mastocytosis. The alteration class and exact variant must be assessed in the disease context.

germline_associations.mechanism: Autosomal dominant; definitive GenCC assertion from ClinGen. Allele-specific mechanism requires review.

function.text: ASXL1 encodes a chromatin-regulatory protein involved in controlling histone modifications and transcriptional programs, including those governing hematopoietic differentiation. Based in part on similarity, it functions as a coactivator of RARA and RXRA through association with NCOA1. It functions as a corepressor for PPARG and suppresses its adipocyte differentiation-inducing activity. It functions as a sensor of N(6)-methyladenine methylation on DNA (6mA): recognizes and binds 6mA DNA, leading to its ubiquitination and degradation by TRIP12, thereby inactivating the PR-DUB complex and regulating Polycomb silencing.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with Bohring-Opitz syndrome (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving ASXL1 have been reported in MDS/MPN, NOS, primary myelofibrosis, and systemic mastocytosis.
